column1: # scripts/ci-test-history.tsv — which test namespaces have failed on CI more than once.
# `namespace<TAB>count`.  scripts/ci-shard.sh reads it, for both legs, to choose the
# ORDER a shard runs its namespaces in.  It never changes which shard a namespace is
# in: the weights files alone decide that.
# The order, policy 1: a shard runs its namespaces by recurring-failure count
# descending, then by the leg's weight (the seconds the namespace is predicted to
# take) descending, then by name ascending.  A namespace this file does not name
# counts 0.  So a namespace that keeps failing reports first, and among the rest the
# expensive ones start early.
# `count` is the number of distinct head commits on which at least one test in the
# namespace failed, over the window below.  A namespace is listed when it is
# recurring: it failed on two or more distinct head commits, or on two or more pull
# requests.  A count is a non-negative whole number; a namespace is spelled as the
# tree spells it (`vaelii.foo-test`).  A row naming a namespace the tree no longer
# has is skipped.
# The two `key: value` lines below are read; every other `#` line is prose.
# `policy` must be the version scripts/ci-shard.sh implements and `status` must be
# `current`.  Anything else — the file missing, `status: stale`, another policy, no
# rows, or one row that is not `namespace<TAB>count` — and ci-shard.sh ignores the
# whole file and runs the order it ran before this file existed (lightest, heaviest,
# second lightest, ...).  No shard loses or gains a namespace either way.
# The file is checked in so that every shard of a run, and any later replay of that
# run, reads the same numbers: CI fetches no history of its own.  Regenerate it by
# hand from the window's failed runs and move the window line with it, or set
# `status: stale` when the numbers are too old to trust.
# Window: vaelii/vaelii upstream CI (.github/workflows/test.yml), runs since 2026-11-02.
# policy: 1
# status: current
